upstream.title: OpenRCA 2.0: From Outcome Labels to Causal Process Supervision
upstream.extraction: pdftotext in reading order, without -layout; each quote checked verbatim against the flattened text of that extraction. The formulas are in Appendix G, which this corpus does not quote -- the definitions it does quote are the ones a reader can hold a rule to without the appendix.
upstream.releasedCode: none found. The microsoft/OpenRCA repository at the pinned commit of the 1.0 evaluator carries evaluate.py for 1.0 only: its README does not mention 2.0 or PAVE at all, and the string 'open-sourced' appears nowhere in the paper or that README.

clauses.quote: Exact Match (EM) requires the predicted set to match ground truth exactly; F1, Precision, and Recall are mean fractional scores over the (service, fault_kind) pair set;
clauses.why: The outcome layer, in one sentence. EM is set equality over (service, fault_kind) pairs -- not a per-facet average -- and F1/Precision/Recall are defined over the same pair set, so for a submission that names exactly one root cause all four are the same number.

clauses.quote: AnySvc is the case-level rate of naming at least one correct root-cause service ignoring fault kind, the most lenient outcome score and a service-only relaxation of Recall.
clauses.why: A published metric that ignores the fault kind. It is the one number this contract can compute that a facet average could not express: right service, wrong kind.

clauses.quote: Node F1 and Edge F1 score the predicted causal graph Ĝ against G ∗ under exact matching;
clauses.why: The process layer's graph comparison. Exact matching means a node or an edge is either in both sets or in one, which is computable from the exported path without the topology -- and it is where partial credit belongs, instead of a facet average that also pays for the root cause a second time.

clauses.quote: The process layer scores the agent’s reasoning: Path Reachability (PR) is satisfied when the agent both names at least one correct root-cause service and draws a valid path through its predicted causal graph from that service to a ground-truth alarm node, a component observed to behave abnormally during the injection window;
clauses.why: The one published process metric this contract cannot compute: PR needs the set of ground-truth alarm nodes, which the PAVE annotation carries and this exporter does not. Recorded as a gap rather than approximated by the graph F1, which is a different quantity.

clauses.quote: We reserve the term ungrounded diagnosis for cases that satisfy AnySvc but not PR: a correct root-cause identification not grounded in a verified causal propagation path to the observed symptom.
clauses.why: Why the layers are reported apart. The paper's own headline finding is that a correct service named without a verified path is the common failure, and a single averaged number hides exactly that: `anySvc` 1 beside `nodeF1` 0 is the sentence.

notImplemented.why: needs the ground-truth alarm nodes the PAVE annotation carries and this export does not; deriving them from the chain would be a different metric wearing its name
